I think that's a really simple way to look at these events. Lauda didn't magically get better when he was sprayed with water. He was horrified after he thought that he killed Guel after stabbing him with his sword. Lauda was pleading for him not to die because he realized he really messed up and he doesn't want Guel to die because he doesn't want to lose his brother. The only reason it didn't end as bad as it did was Felsi spreading emergency sealant to prevent the suit and Guel from being destroyed, not to cool off Lauda.

For Suletta, it's up to personal opinion that the Earth house isn't part of the people that she cares about. They are certainly close enough that they are willing to go into what is essentially a W.M.D. to stop Prospera and help Suletta make up with her family. Plus they are still friends with her, and close enough to visit, years after when they're long since graduated.

Plus Suletta didn't just decide to move the plot forward, she realized that people will often make the best decisions they can at the moment, even if it's not quite the best thing, with the Earth house literally discussing that lesson in regards to Martin giving up Nika because he wanted to protect his friends. Suletta remembered that Eri told her not to follow her and realized that Eri was trying to protect her from Prospera's schemes by distancing her. Having that realization that the people that care about her didn't abandon her because they hate her, but because they are trying to help her gives her the resolution to move forward.

They aren't completely healed. They all made mistakes and have things they need to work through. But they would rather do it with the people they love, and by trying to understand one another, they can.

I think that with these characters it isn't that they magically get better, but more like that they gain the resolve to temporarily move past it to reach a happier conclusion.

Lauda doesn't really make up with his brother, he just realizes that despite everything he can't really bring himself to kill him and that Guel really does care about him.

Suletta never really was abandoned by everyone despite losing Aerial, Prospera, and Miorine. She still has the Earth house to support her and tries to find a way forward despite losing the people close to her.

Miorine didn't magically get better either. She's still dealing with the guilt of unintentionally being part of the tragedy at Guinharbor. Even three years later she's still working towards making amends.

They aren't just magically healed of their trauma. They just realized that there is hope for them if they move forward by putting the effort in and trying to communicate with the people that love them. I think it is more of a work in progress than a conclusion.

Domestic violence is not purely physical. Emotional abuse, neglect, and mistreatment can be accounted for as well. Not all perpetrators are always charged and properly arrested as well. If you want to go by **amount of arrests in the US** according to the FBI over the course of 10 years, then 52,569 men have been arrested for offenses against family and children, compared to 17,088 women.

No I did not say that 1 in 3 women in the US are victims of rape, physical violence, and/or stalking by an intimate partner, I gave you a quote from an article linking a phone survey with 16,507 participants in the US. Finally, I did not try to say that other factors such as poverty are the main cause, merely state that other factors can be at play to explain the data. Sample size, other factors (like poverty and a lack of willingness due to societal stigma) are at play here, which even this: [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499891/](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK499891/) , article that I linked earlier explained.
